audit_questions.challenge: Did M18 introduce complex sync orchestration or offline queue managers?
audit_questions.finding: No. NetworkConnectivityMonitor is a lightweight callback adapter wrapping standard Android ConnectivityManager.registerNetworkCallback and iOS NWPathMonitor. Zero complex offline sync workers, job schedulers, or background sync engines.

audit_questions.challenge: Did M18 build complex custom disk caching mechanisms?
audit_questions.finding: No. Leverages platform-native caches (Coil disk LRU on Android, URLCache on iOS). WeatherCacheStore uses single Android SharedPreferences / iOS UserDefaults file with standard key-value pairs.

audit_questions.challenge: Did M18 create redundant databases or duplicate place models?
audit_questions.finding: No. Reused existing M14 SavedPlaceEntity (Room) and SavedPlaceModel (SwiftData) directly with zero schema migrations.

audit_questions.challenge: Did M18 start aggressive polling threads or battery-draining services?
audit_questions.finding: No. Relies purely on passive OS network callback events without background services, wakelocks, or recurring polling alarms.

audit_questions.challenge: Did M18 invent bloated multi-layer wrappers?
audit_questions.finding: No. Pure dual-native idiomatic Compose / SwiftUI implementations with minimal glue.
